Leo Park: Quick sync — customer asked for "canonical" audit events for Private deployments + S3 export. They want fields that map straight into their SIEM. What’s the minimal mandatory set we guarantee?
Maya Singh: Do they require tenant display name or just tenant_id? We should avoid leaking any PII into S3 objects.
Tom Rivera: Current minimal payload for webhook looks like: tenant_id, user_id, action, resource, timestamp, request_id. We do not include KMS key material or plaintext tenant names.
Maya Singh: For SIEM compatibility we should add event_type and severity and provide a CEF mapping doc. Datadog wants a top-level service and status fields.
Tom Rivera: Re: KMS metadata — customers asked whether we can surface key_alias or key_id in the audit event when using envelope encryption. We can include key_alias (masked) but not key material or encryption_context values that may contain PII.
Leo Park: Agree on masked key_alias. Also propose adding delivery_status metadata so they can trace whether S3 export / webhook attempt succeeded: delivery:{protocol, endpoint, status, attempts, last_error}.
Sam (audit-bot): Posted draft schema v1.1 here: https://redwood.internal/schemas/audit-events/v1.1 (preview). Includes delivery metadata + pseudonymization flag.
Tom Rivera: For onboarding: we should provide sample payloads for Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs, and a CEF example. Also a small replay tool so customers can validate parsing on their side.
Maya Singh: Security note: S3 exports currently write JSON lines unencrypted at rest in customer's bucket by default. For Private deployments we need to ensure the docs highlight KMS envelope + SSE-S3 vs SSE-KMS options and recommend SSE-KMS with envelope for regulated customers.
Leo Park: Also add a pseudonymize option — store hashed_tenant_id and remove tenant_display_name unless customer explicitly opts in. That solves a lot of compliance concerns.
Tom Rivera: Example sample we can share with customers during onboarding:
```
{
  "event_type": "model.eval.run",
  "ts": "2025-02-05T15:12:03Z",
  "tenant_id": "sha256:abcd...",
  "user_id": "u-1234",
  "resource": "dedicated/cluster-07",
  "delivery": { "protocol": "s3", "bucket": "acme-audit", "status": "ok" }
}
```
Maya Singh: Validation flow for onboarding: 1) we provide sample payload set, 2) they map fields in their SIEM, 3) they run replay against their ingestion (we provide replay token), 4) they confirm mapping + we sign off. Add X-RD-AUDIT-SIG header for webhooks so customers can verify authenticity.
Ash (oncall-bot): Created onboarding ticket RDW-9876 and incident stub RDINC-1234 for an earlier delivery schema mismatch — linked to this thread.
Tom Rivera: Action items: I’ll draft schema diff, CEF/Datadog/Splunk examples, and a short onboarding playbook.
Maya Singh: I’ll draft the KMS exposure policy (what metadata is allowed). Add a small checklist: pseudonymization, SSE-KMS recommended, signature header required for webhooks, replay token for validation.
Leo Park: Can we also include a short paragraph in the Console UI next to the export toggle explaining these tradeoffs? Many customers miss the KMS settings on first pass.
Maya Singh: Good call — I'll add copy to the Console team ticket.
Leo Park: Thanks all — please put estimates on RDW-9876 by EOD. :thumbsup:
Sam (audit-bot): Reminder: schema review meeting scheduled Thu 10:00am.
_meta: This thread is an internal eng-security discussion about audit event schema, KMS metadata exposure, S3 export onboarding, SIEM mappings, and customer validation flow. Contains action items and a sample payload for onboarding.
